title: Large Scale Synthesis of Native Turn and Helix Mimics Stabilized by a Generic Hydrogen Bond Surrogate
protocol: Take 3.35 g of Cbz-S(tBu)-OH in an oven-dried 100 ml RBF containing a Teflon-coated magnetic stir bar.
Seal the RBF with rubber septum and wrap it with parafilm.
Evacuate the flask using high vacuum for 2 min via an inlet needle.
Backfill the flask with N₂ balloon through a needle.
Add 23 ml dry THF to the reaction mixture via syringe equipped with aspiration needle.
Stir the reaction mixture at -15°C for 1 hour and 30 minutes.
Seal the RBF with rubber septum and wrap it with parafilm again.
Subsequently, connect a H₂N-N(Trt)-OMe solution to the RBF through a needle.
Repeat steps of evacuation and backfilling twice.
Make a solution by adding 10 ml dry THF via syringe equipped with aspiration needle.
Add 1.55 ml of N-Methylmorpholine (NMM) in a disposable syringe equipped with a stainless-steel needle while stirring the reaction mixture at -15°C.
Add 0.95 ml of ethyl chloroformate (ECF) in a disposable syringe equipped with a stainless-steel needle.
Transfer the solution of H₂N-N(Trt)-OMe using syringe equipped with aspiration needle to the RBF containing Cbz-S(tBu)-OH solution.
Add 2.6 ml of NMM in a disposable syringe equipped with a stainless-steel needle over a period of 30 sec.
Let the reaction mixture stir at -15°C for 1.5 h.
Monitor the reaction progress by TLC (70% vol/vol ethyl acetate : pet ether) and HRMS.
Do the qualitative estimation of the starting material and the product during the reaction.
Quench the reaction by adding a few drops of double-distilled water; the solution should turn from turbid to clear.
Remove THF using a rotary evaporator under a low-pressure gradient (400 – 800 mbar) with a water bath temperature set at 48°C.
Transfer the reaction mixture dissolved in 20-30 ml ethyl acetate to a 100 ml separatory funnel and add 1N HCl slowly (10ml / 30 sec).
Seal the separatory funnel with a polyethylene cap, shake the reaction mixture, and let it settle for 2 minutes until two layers separate.
If no clear separation occurs, add more ethyl acetate until there is (~10 ml) clear separation of layers.
Separate the aqueous layer from the organic layer.
Add saturated sodium bicarbonate (10 ml) to the organic layer.
Seal the separatory funnel again with a polyethylene cap, shake the reaction mixture, and let it settle for 2 minutes until two layers are separated.
Separate the aqueous layer.
Pass the organic layer through crystalline sodium sulfate to remove residual water.
Collect the treated organic layer in a 100 ml one-neck round-bottom flask.
Repeat steps 14-16 twice with EtOAc, discarding the aqueous layer each time.
Remove the organic portion in a rotary evaporator at 45°C and vacuum pressure gradient of 400 – 800 mbar to obtain a transparent liquid compound.
Dissolve the residue in minimum amount of DCM (2 ml) and add 5 g silica gel (100 – 200 mesh).
Remove DCM under high vacuum (100 mbar) to obtain dry slurry.
Pack a chromatography column with dimensions L - 400 mm, D - 30 mm using dry silica gel (100 – 200 mesh).
Transfer the dry slurry directly to the packed column using a plastic funnel (D - 55 mm).
Elute the desired product using EtOAc/pet. ether in a ratio of 50% vol/vol through gravity column at a rate of 400 ml/1h.
Collect the fraction in 25 x 150 mm test tubes.
Identify the fractions containing the desired product using TLC and visualize it with UV lamp (254 nm).
Combine the identified fractions in 500 ml round-bottom flask (RBF).
Remove the solvent from RBF by rotary evaporator, setting water bath temperature to 48°C.
Dry the compound using oil vacuum pump at 10 mbar pressure to obtain a white solid compound.
Attach an N₂ balloon to the reaction flask.
Take 0.36 g of Boc-A-OH in an oven-dried 50 ml round-bottomed flask (RBF).
Seal the RBF with a rubber septum and wrap it with parafilm.
Evacuate the flask using high vacuum for 5 min via an inlet needle.
Backfill the flask with N₂ through a needle.
Repeat steps of evacuation and backfilling twice.
Add 10 ml dry THF to the solution via a 10 ml syringe equipped with an aspiration needle.
Stir the reaction mixture at -15°C for 1.5 hours.
Add 262 μl of N-methyl morpholine (NMM) in a Hamilton microsyringe to the solution.
Next, add 160 μl of ethyl chloroformate (ECF) via a Hamilton microsyringe; the reaction mixture turns clear to turbid.
After 4-5 min, transfer the TFA-R(Z₂)-Ipr solution using an aspiration needle-equipped syringe to the RBF containing Boc-A-OH and ECF solution.
Immediately add 436 μl of NMM in a Hamilton microsyringe to the reaction mixture.
Let the reaction mixture stir at -15°C for 1.5 hours.
Check the TLC for full consumption of acid in the form of corresponding ester.
Monitor the reaction progress by TLC and HRMS.
Perform qualitative estimation of starting material and product during the reaction.
Quench the reaction with few drops of double-distilled water.
Remove THF by rotary evaporation under a low-pressure gradient (400 – 800 mbar) with water bath temperature set at 48°C.
Transfer the reaction mixture to a separatory funnel after dissolving in ethyl acetate (EtOAc).
Add 1N HCl slowly (10ml / 30 sec).
Seal the separatory funnel with a polyethylene cap.
Shake the reaction mixture until two layers are separated out.
If no clear separation occurs, add more EtOAc (~10 ml).
Separate the aqueous layer and discard it.
Add 5 ml of saturated sodium bicarbonate to the organic layer.
Seal the separatory funnel again with a polyethylene cap.
Shake the reaction mixture until two layers are separated out.
Separate the aqueous layer and pass the organic layer through crystalline sodium sulfate.
Collect the organic layer in a 100 ml one-neck round-bottom flask (RBF).
Repeat steps involving EtOAc twice more, discarding the aqueous layer each time.
Remove the organic portion using a rotary evaporator to obtain a white solid compound.
Set the water bath temperature to 48°C and vacuum pressure gradient from 400 to 800 mbar.
Dissolve the residue in a minimum amount of DCM (2 ml).
Add 1 g of silica gel (100-200 mesh) to the solution.
Remove the DCM in high vacuum (100 mbar) to obtain a dry slurry.
Pack the chromatography column with dry silica gel (L – 300 mm, D - 30 mm).
Transfer the dry slurry to the column using a plastic funnel (D - 55 mm).
Elute the desired product using EtOAc/pet. ether (70% vol/vol) by gravity column at a rate of 400 ml/1h.
Collect the fraction in 18 x 125 mm test tubes.
Identify the fractions containing the desired product with TLC and visualize it with UV lamp (254 nm).
Combine the fractions containing the desired product in 100 ml RBF.
Remove the solvent by rotary evaporator at a water bath temperature of 48°C.
Dry the compound using oil vacuum pump (10 mbar) to obtain a white solid compound.
Dissolve 50 mg of ninhydrin in 500 ml of ethanol to make a 1% w/v solution.
Perform analytical TLC on pre-coated TLC plates with silica gel 60 F<sub>254</sub>.
Spray the TLC plate with the 1% ninhydrin solution.
Heat the TLC plate on a hot plate at 120°C for 30 seconds.
Perform analytical TLC on pre-coated TLC plates with silica gel 60 F<sub>254</sub>.
Place solid I<sub>2</sub> in a wide-mouth glass jar with a lid.
Heat the TLC plate on a hot plate at 120°C for 30 seconds.
Keep the TLC plate in an iodine chamber for 5 minutes.
Perform analytical TLC on pre-coated TLC plates with silica gel 60 F<sub>254</sub>.
Visualize the TLC plate under UV light (254 nm).
Transfer 10 g of Ns-G-OMe and 14.3 g triphenylphosphine in an oven-dried RBF containing a Teflon-coated magnetic stir bar.
Seal the RBF with a rubber septum and wrap it with parafilm.
Evacuate the flask using high vacuum for 2 min via an inlet needle.
Backfill the flask with N₂ balloon through a needle.
Add 125 ml dry THF to the reaction mixture via a syringe equipped with an aspiration needle.
Place the RBF in an ice bath and maintain the temperature at 0°C for the next hour, allowing the mixture to stir until everything dissolves.
Mix 10.8 ml of diisopropyl azodicarboxylate (DIAD) with the reaction mixture dropwise over a period of 5 min.
Stir the reaction mixture at room temperature for 1 hour.
Monitor the reaction progress by TLC and HRMS.
Quench the reaction by adding few drops of double-distilled water.
Remove THF by rotary evaporator under low-pressure gradient (400 – 800 mbar).
Maintain the reaction flask in the rotary evaporator for an additional 10 – 15 minutes to remove residual water.
Add 125 ml of ACN and stir at room temperature.
Add 10.1 g of potassium carbonate (73 mmol, 1 eq.) to the stirring mixture.
Then add 5.6 ml of thiophenol (54.8 mmol, 1.5 eq.), continue stirring for 18 hours.
Monitor reaction progress by TLC using 80% ethyl acetate and pet. ether as solvents.
Perform qualitative estimation of starting material and product during the reaction.
Remove acetonitrile using a rotary evaporator under a low-pressure gradient (400 – 800 mbar) with water bath temperature set at 48°C.
Acidify the reaction mixture to pH 2 – 3 by adding 3N HCl in an ice bath (0°C).
Transfer the reaction mixture into a separatory funnel after dissolving it in 10 ml diethyl ether.
Seal the separatory funnel with a polyethylene cap, shake the mixture and let settle for 2 minutes until layers separate clearly.
Add more diethyl ether if separation is not clear (~10 ml total).
Discard the organic layer and retain the aqueous layer after separation.
Repeat steps involving separation using diethyl ether several times as needed.
Use TLC (ethyl acetate/pet. ether (80% (vol/vol))) to check the purity of the product.
Use ^1H NMR to confirm the purity of the product.
Collect the aqueous portion containing compound 3 in a 250 ml round-bottom flask.
Place the collected solution in an ice bath at 0°C.
Basify the solution using sodium bicarbonate until pH reaches 11 – 12.
Check the pH of the basified solution using pH paper.
Take 9.2 ml of Di-tert-butyl decarbonate ((Boc)₂O) using a 20 ml disposable syringe with an aspiration needle (20 Gaze x 12 Inch).
Pour 60 ml of THF into another 100 ml pear-shaped flask.
Transfer the (Boc)₂O solution to the reaction mixture while stirring.
Remove the ice bath after 30 minutes and allow the reaction mixture to stir for 12 hours.
Monitor the reaction progress by TLC (50% vol/vol ethyl acetate : pet. ether).
Submit 1 mg of the crude product in a 1.5 ml Eppendorf vial for HRMS analysis.
Continue stirring until TLC and HRMS show no traces of N-(HCl-propyl alcohol)-G-OMe (3).
Qualitatively estimate the starting material and product during the reaction.
Remove THF by rotary evaporator under a low-pressure gradient of 400 to 800 mbar with water bath temperature set at 48°C.

Transfer the reaction mixture after dissolving in 30 ml EtOAc into a 100 ml separatory funnel, seal with polyethylene cap, shake and let settle for 2 min until layers separate clearly or add more EtOAc if separation is not clear (~10 ml).
Separate the aqueous layer from the organic layer.
Pass the organic layer through crystalline sodium sulfate to remove residual water and collect in a 100 ml one-neck round-bottom flask (RBF).
Extract the aqueous part twice with EtOAc (2 x 20 ml) and discard the aqueous layer after each extraction.
Evaporate the organic portion in a rotary evaporator at water bath temperature of 45°C and vacuum pressure gradient of 400 to 800 mbar until a transparent liquid compound is obtained.
Dissolve the residue in a minimum amount of DCM (5 ml) and add 10-15 g silica gel (100–200 mesh).
Remove DCM under high vacuum (100 mbar) to obtain a dry slurry.
Pack a chromatography column with dimensions L - 300 mm, D - 43 mm using dry silica gel (100-200 mesh).
Directly transfer the dry slurry to the column using a plastic funnel (D - 55 mm).

Combine all the fractions in 25 x 150 mm test tubes.
Using the TLC, identify the fractions containing the desired product and visualize by ninhydrin test.
Combine the fractions containing the desired product in 500 ml RBF.
Remove the solvent by rotary evaporator with water bath temperature set to 48°C.
Dry the compound using oil vacuum pump (10 mbar) to obtain the compound as yellowish oil.

Transfer 4.8 g of Ns-A-OBn (13.2 mmol, 1 eq.), 4.88 g of N-(Boc-propyl alcohol)-G-OMe (19.8 mmol, 1.5 eq.) and 5.18 g of triphenylphosphine (PPh₃) (19.8 mmol, 1.5 eq.) in an oven-dried 100 ml round-bottom flask containing a Teflon-coated magnetic stir bar.

Repeat steps of evacuation and backfilling twice.
Add 44 ml dry THF via a 50 ml syringe equipped with an aspiration needle (20 Gauge x 12 Inch).
Put the round RBF into the ice bath to maintain the temperature of the reaction mixture at -15°C for 30 min and allow stirring until everything is dissolved.
Add 3.91 ml of diisopropyl azodicarboxylate (DIAD) dropwise over a period of 3 min using a disposable syringe equipped with a stainless-steel needle.
Stir the reaction mixture at room temperature for 45 min after adding DIAD.
Monitor the reaction progress by TLC and HRMS, ensuring no traces of N-(Boc-propyl alcohol)-G-OMe are present.
Quench the reaction by adding a few drops of double-distilled water.
Remove THF using a rotary evaporator under a low-pressure gradient (400 – 800 mbar) with a water bath set at 48°C.
Keep the round-bottom flask in the rotary evaporator for an additional 10 – 15 minutes to remove residual water.
Add 44 ml of ACN and start stirring at room temperature.
Add 10.1 g of potassium carbonate (26.4 mmol, 2 eq.).
Add 2.03 ml of thiophenol (19.8 mmol, 1.5 eq.) and stir the reaction mixture for 8 hours.
Monitor the reaction progress by TLC using a solvent system of 80% ethyl acetate : pet. ether.
Remove acetonitrile by rotary evaporator under low-pressure gradient (400 – 800 mbar) and set water bath temperature at 48°C.
Acidify the reaction mixture under ice bath with 1N HCl until pH reaches 2 – 3.
Transfer the reaction mixture after dissolving in 10 ml diethyl ether to a separatory funnel, seal it, shake well, and let settle for 2 min.
Add more Et₂O if no clear separation occurs until there is (~10 ml) clear separation.
Separate the aqueous layer and discard the organic layer.
Extract the aqueous portion with diethyl ether several times until TLC confirms the complete removal of impurities.
Use TLC (ethyl acetate/pet. ether (80%)) and ¹H NMR to check the purity of the compound.
Collect the aqueous portion in a 250 ml round-bottom flask, keep it in an ice bath at 0°C, and basify using sodium bicarbonate until pH reaches 11 – 12.
Take 2.56 ml of methoxycarbonyl chloride using a disposable syringe equipped with an aspiration needle, pour 20 ml of THF into another container.
Transfer the methoxycarbonyl chloride solution to the reaction mixture while stirring.
Monitor the reaction progress by TLC (50% vol/vol ethyl acetate : pet. ether) and HRMS after removing the ice bath and allowing the reaction to stir for 10 hours.
Take 1 mg of the crude product in a 1.5 ml Eppendorf vial.
Submit for mass spectrum analysis.
Perform qualitative estimation of starting material and product during reaction by following steps A, B, C (mentioned in BOX3).

Open the bottle inside the well-vented hood.

Monitor the reaction progress every 1 hour by TLC using 50% vol/vol ethyl acetate and pet. ether.

Remove excess TFA and DCM using short path distillation set up.
Dry the compound using oil vacuum pump at 10 mbar to obtain N-(TFA-propyl alcohol)-G-OMe-N-(Moc-propyl alcohol)-A-OBn as a reddish oil.

Backfill the flask with N₂ balloon through a needle (0.8 x 25 mm).

Remove excess TFA and DCM using short path distillation set up.
Dry the compound under oil vacuum pump at 10 mbar to obtain the product.
Dissolve 0.15 g of Moc-[ASN]G-AR(Z₂)-Ipr in 1 ml of MeOH.
Add 15 mg of Pd/C to the solution.
Fill the reaction bottle with H₂ gas using an H₂ balloon.
Stir the mixture for 30 minutes at room temperature.
Filter off the Pd/C using GE Whatman – 42 filter paper and collect the filtrate in a 20 ml round-bottom flask (RBF).
Remove MeOH from the solution using a rotary evaporator with water bath set to 48°C and pressure gradient 400–800 mbar.
Dry the compound using an oil vacuum pump at 10 mbar to obtain 0.11 g of Moc-[ASN]G-AR-Ipr as a white solid.
Dissolve 50 mg crude Moc-[ASN]G-AR-Ipr compound in a mixture of 5 ml ACN and 5 ml water.
Inject the solution into the semipreparative HPLC system.
Collect fractions corresponding to the main peak.
Lyophilize the aqueous fraction to obtain the purified product.
